decision: Use a bounded automatic lease-heartbeat loop inside WorkerRuntime.runOnce and fail closed before completion if heartbeat authority is lost.
problem: WorkerRuntime now carries per-claim fencing tokens, but long-running execute callbacks can still outlive the queue lease unless every executor remembers to call the manual heartbeat control. That makes correct long-running work vulnerable to lease expiry/reclaim and stale completion conflicts.

correctness.preferred: automatic lease renewal tied to the claimed mission lifecycle
correctness.reason: lease ownership remains valid independently of executor-specific heartbeat discipline, and completion is blocked if automatic renewal fails

robustness_security.preferred: fail closed on heartbeat failure while retaining the original fencing token
robustness_security.reason: a worker must never report success after lease authority becomes uncertain; stale/fenced failure remains visible instead of silently committing

latency_resources_regression.preferred: local timer with one serialized coordinator heartbeat per interval, defaulting to roughly one third of lease duration
latency_resources_regression.reason: no new network, Qubes, daemon, store, or protocol dependency; quick tasks usually complete before the first timer fires, while long tasks pay bounded durable-heartbeat cost

alternatives.name: manual heartbeat only
alternatives.rejected: correctness depends on every executor remembering lease maintenance; omission causes avoidable lease expiry

alternatives.name: extend leases to very large fixed durations
alternatives.rejected: reduces recovery responsiveness after crashes and weakens stale-worker fencing

alternatives.name: external heartbeat daemon
alternatives.rejected: adds lifecycle, IPC/network, resource, and regression surface before Qubes transport is introduced

qa: long synthetic execution spans multiple lease periods and still completes under requireLeaseToken=true
synthetic automatic-heartbeat failure prevents complete() from being called and routes the mission through fail-closed failure handling
existing manual heartbeat, restart/session fencing, same-session stale-token fencing, retry, and capability tests remain in the Mission Runtime suite
resource_notes: Default heartbeat interval is approximately leaseMs/3 with a 10ms floor. The timer is unref'd so it does not keep a worker process alive. No extra durable mutation occurs for tasks that finish before the first interval.
failure_lessons: A fencing token is necessary but not sufficient for long work: the worker must also maintain lease liveness.
Heartbeat failure must be treated as lost authority, not as telemetry noise.
Automatic renewal should be stopped and awaited before terminal completion to avoid a heartbeat racing with completion.
